title: Maze and Subset Problems
description: Explore how Backtracking solves pathfinding and subset exploration problems through recursive search.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Backtracking is highly effective for pathfinding and subset exploration problems.

Maze solving and subset generation demonstrate how recursive exploration can systematically examine possible paths while avoiding invalid decisions.

sections.title: Maze Solving with Backtracking
sections.content:
Maze-solving algorithms attempt to find a valid path from a starting point to a destination.

The algorithm explores possible directions recursively while tracking visited locations.

If a path reaches a dead end, the algorithm backtracks and explores alternative routes.

sections.title: Recursive Path Exploration
sections.content:
At every step, the algorithm evaluates possible movements such as moving up, down, left, or right.

Valid paths are explored recursively, while blocked or previously visited cells are rejected.

This systematic exploration eventually discovers valid paths if they exist.

sections.title: Subset Problems
sections.content:
Subset problems involve generating all possible subsets from a collection of elements.

For every element, the algorithm decides whether to include or exclude it.

This repeated branching process produces all possible combinations systematically.

sections.title: The Decision Tree Structure
sections.content:
Subset generation can be visualized as a decision tree.

Every branch represents a choice to include or exclude an element.

Backtracking explores each branch recursively until all possible subsets have been generated.

sections.title: Pathfinding and Subset Problems in Real Applications
sections.content:
Pathfinding algorithms are used in robotics, navigation systems, video games, and autonomous vehicles.

Subset exploration appears in recommendation systems, optimization problems, financial analysis, and machine learning.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Backtracking efficiently solves maze and subset problems through recursive exploration, rollback, and systematic decision-making. These techniques form the foundation of many pathfinding and optimization systems.
